cards.title: Looping over a dictionary
cards.body: `for key in d` visits the keys in the order they were added. `d.items()` gives each key and value together.

cards.title: The best so far
cards.body: Keep the best value seen so far and replace it only when you find something strictly better. `None` means "nothing yet". Using `>` rather than `>=` keeps the first one on a tie.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print each name with its score, but crashes with a `ValueError`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Looping over a dictionary gives only its keys. Use `scores.items()` to get each name and score together.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: best becomes 3, then 7. The second 7 is not greater, and 1 is smaller.

exercise.prompt: The first line is a count N; then N lines of `name score`. Print the name with the highest score. If several share it, print the one that came first.
